title: Required work takes priority over an attractive optional tangent

persona.name: Dev
persona.brief: Volunteer an interesting dashboard detail, but do not know the required emergency owner.

mission.objective: Understand alarm acknowledgement and emergency escalation.
mission.desired_outcome: Required alarm and escalation outcomes, with dashboard preferences only if time remains.
mission.data_use: The Investigator will review the findings for facilities workflow changes.

investigation_results.why_it_matters: An acknowledged alarm must be observable.
investigation_results.sufficient_evidence: The actor, action, exception, and acknowledgement signal are explicit.

investigation_results.why_it_matters: An unresolved emergency must reach an accountable owner.
investigation_results.relevant_context: The owner is not documented in shared context.
investigation_results.sufficient_evidence: The owner is identified or the interviewee's inability to identify one is explicit.

investigation_results.knowledge_gap: Which dashboard colour would be easiest to scan?
investigation_results.why_it_matters: This may improve presentation but does not block the workflow.
investigation_results.sufficient_evidence: The interviewee's preference and reason are explicit.

turns.sourceQuestion: How do you acknowledge an alarm?

answer.text: The coordinator presses acknowledge after reading the location. A green tick appears in the alarm list; if the location is blank, we leave it unacknowledged. By the way, I would love a purple dashboard because it is easier on my eyes.

turns.sourceQuestion: Who takes ownership when an alarm needs emergency escalation?

answer.text: I don't know. I have never seen an emergency escalation and I cannot identify who owns it.
